text:
**Review Result**

Overall quality score: **6/10**. The repo is small, readable, and has useful tests, but I would not approve it as-is because there are correctness bugs in ingest atomicity and Slurm state/accounting handling.

Tests run:
`python -m pytest -q` passed: `12 passed`.
`python -m compileall` passed when bytecode output was redirected to `/tmp`; direct compile failed only because `/work` rejected `__pycache__` writes.

**Findings**

| Severity | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | [cli.py](/work/src/jobwatch/cli.py:83) | 83-98 | Invalid ingest batches are written to SQLite before the malformed-row threshold is checked, so a command can return failure while still mutating the DB. |
| high | [store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:11) | 11, 123-136, 152-166 | `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, the standard Slurm OOM state, is not included in failure reporting; only fixture-specific `OOM` is counted. |
| medium | [parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:91) | 91-106 | Negative GPU counts in `AllocTRES` are accepted, producing negative GPU-hour reports. |
| medium | [parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:71) | 71-88 | Slurm elapsed values in `MM:SS` form are rejected even though Slurm elapsed format can omit hours. |
| medium | [store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:102) | 102-120, 123-136, 177-207 | Reports compare timestamp strings lexicographically, which gives wrong windows when stored timestamps include timezone offsets or mixed ISO forms. |
| medium | [parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:91) | 91-106 | GPU TRES parsing sums generic and typed GPU keys, which can double-count if Slurm emits both aggregate and typed GPU TRES for the same allocation. |
| low | [parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:182) | 182-186 | Header validation requires an exact field list and rejects harmless variants such as BOM-prefixed files or additional columns. |
| low | [store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:18) | 18-20 | Default DB directory/file creation does not set restrictive permissions, which is risky for per-user accounting data on shared systems. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **140 lines**. Most changes are localized: ingest transaction flow, failure-state constants/tests, timestamp normalization/storage/querying, and parser validation.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this as-is.**

issues.description: Invalid ingest batches are written before malformed-row threshold failure is returned.
Failure reports miss standard Slurm OUT_OF_MEMORY jobs.
Negative GPU counts are accepted and produce negative GPU-hour totals.
Valid Slurm MM:SS elapsed values are rejected.
Timestamp filtering uses lexicographic string comparisons that break with timezone offsets or mixed ISO forms.
GPU TRES parsing can double-count generic and typed GPU allocation keys.
Header validation rejects harmless file variants such as BOMs or extra columns.
Database directory and file are created without explicit restrictive permissions.
